claim: For every fixed finite r,s>=1, every fixed finite k_ji>=1, and every fixed strictly positive finite rate vector alpha_j, delta_j, p_ji, q_ji, u_ji, v_ji on the complete-pair family in foster_multicatalyst.txt, the stochastic mass-action CTMC on N_0^(r+s) is irreducible, nonexplosive, and positive recurrent.
assumptions: Each ordered catalyst-substrate pair (j,i) has both displayed substrate/autocatalysis reversible pairs (four directed reactions), with strictly positive finite constants.
Propensities use falling factorials for repeated reactants.
The rate vector is fixed; this is not a uniform-in-parameters assertion.
proof_object: REPORT.txt, Sections 1-3: exact generator for V=sum_j lambda_j a_j+sum_i R_i^b_i+K 1_{A=0}; choose lambda_j>0 and R_i>1 with lambda_j delta_j-sum_i p_ji(R_i-1)>0; q_ji>0 gives g_ji(m)->-infinity; v_ji>0 gives factorial control on every fixed nonzero-substrate stratum. This makes {LV>-1} finite. Localized physical-time Dynkin bounds rule out explosion, and the continuous-time Foster criterion gives positive recurrence.
class_and_invariants: The full lattice is one closed communicating class: each B_i can be cleared with an active catalyst; catalysts can then be drained; immigration and A_j->A_j+B_i build any target, using a temporary catalyst for targets with zero catalysts. The stoichiometric vectors include e_j and e_j+e_Bi-e_j=e_Bi, so the stoichiometric rank is r+s and there are no nonzero linear conservation laws.
stationary_law: A unique invariant probability exists by irreducibility and positive recurrence. It is not characterized in closed form here; no stationary-tail or parameter-uniform tightness claim is made.
supplied_and_acquired: Supplied: finite indices, finite integers k_ji, and fixed positive finite rates. Acquired: positive lambda_j, rational R_i>1 satisfying the displayed strict margins, and K>(sum_j alpha_j lambda_j+1)/sum_j alpha_j. For rational rate inputs, the weight inequalities can be searched and verified exactly; for arbitrary real inputs, certificate selection is existential absent an input-access/precision model.
cost_and_limits: The mathematical proof uses finitely many rate comparisons and a pointwise finite Foster set whose size is not bounded explicitly. The exact script checks a fixed fixture with Fraction arithmetic; it is not needed for the all-state proof. No uniform bound on Foster-set size, expected returns, mixing, or stationary tightness over varying rates is proved.
falsifier: A statewise discrepancy in the generator identity in Section 2, a sequence escaping every finite set on which LV does not tend to -infinity, or an explosion path contradicting the localized physical-time Dynkin bound would refute the claim.

primary_source.citation: D. F. Anderson and J. Kim, Some network conditions for positive recurrence of stochastically modeled reaction networks, arXiv:1710.11263v3 (2018), Theorem 3.1.
primary_source.use: Finite-set continuous-time Foster criterion only; nonexplosion is proved separately here.

novelty_status: No novelty, priority, or external-verification claim. The family-specific proof and its scope require independent expert review.

claim: The exact r=1,s=2,k_1i=1 fixture alpha=delta=p_i=1, q_i=2, u_i=1, v_i=2 is full-rank, weakly reversible, not complex balanced, and violates the supplied strict small-gain LP while being positive recurrent by the complete-pair Foster theorem.
assumptions: All rates use standard stochastic mass action.
proof_object: REPORT.txt, Section 4. LP infeasibility follows from lambda>w1+w2 and 2w_i>lambda for i=1,2. Complex balance would force a=alpha/delta=1 at the 0/A leaf and a=u/v=1/2 at each 2A+B_i leaf. The exact drift witness uses lambda=1,R_1=R_2=6/5,K=3 and finite set F={1<=a<=3,0<=b_1,b_2<=9}.
stationary_law: A unique stationary probability exists, but is not computed in closed form.
status_boundary: This shows failure of the linear certificate is not evidence of nonrecurrence for this family. It is not a transient/null-recurrent/explosive example and makes no assertion about other weakly reversible networks.
falsifier: An exact reaction-generator mismatch or a state outside F with LV>-1 falsifies the displayed fixture certificate; the complete theorem's broader falsifier is recorded in the preceding claim.

claim: validate_exact.py verifies the rational g(m) values and difference identity, independently recomputes the fixture generator from explicit reaction propensities over a 16^3 state box including boundaries, and checks LV<=-1 on a 20,656-state grid outside F.
inputs: Python 3 standard library only; exact Fraction arithmetic.
result: PASS; grid maximum outside F is -7/5.
scope_limit: Finite checks do not establish the analytic all-state drift inequalities, nonexplosion, recurrence, novelty, or external correctness.

claim: For a finite bipartite support E, with positive paired reactions on every edge and positive immigration/death for every catalyst, each communicating class is positive recurrent; the class labels are the fixed counts of isolated substrates.
assumptions: Every included catalyst-substrate edge has all four reversible substrate/autocatalysis reactions with positive finite rates and finite k_ji>=1.
Every catalyst has positive finite 0->A_j and A_j->0 rates.
Isolated substrate coordinates are fixed within a communicating class.
proof_object: Separate file SPARSE_EXTENSION.txt. The proposed V uses R_i^b_i(1+epsilon_i 1_{all neighbors of i absent}) so immigration turns a large inactive-substrate weight down, while last-neighbor death turns it up. The latter is dominated at large b_i by the matched q_ji a_j b_i R_i^b_i term. A mixed-escape subsequence argument also uses the chi_j margin at zero adjacent substrate and reverse factorial terms at fixed positive adjacent substrate.
class_and_invariants: Each isolated B_i count is conserved. Within each fixed vector of isolated counts, immigration/death and the paired edge reactions connect all remaining nonnegative coordinates; if there are no isolated substrates, the full lattice is one class.
scope_limit: This is separate from the complete-pair theorem and has not received independent review. validate_sparse.py checks the exact switching generator on a finite box but does not validate the all-state escape argument. No uniform stationary tightness over varying parameters is proved. Missing reverse edges, zero rates, or non-mass-action rates are outside scope.

claim: validate_sparse.py independently computes the support-corrected Foster generator from explicit reaction propensities and checks equality on a 4096-state boundary-inclusive box for E={(A1,B1),(A2,B1),(A2,B2)}.
inputs: Python 3 standard library Fraction arithmetic; alpha=delta=p=1, q=v=2, u=1, k=1, R=6/5, epsilon=1, K=2.
result: PASS on all states a1,a2,b1,b2 in {0,...,7}.
scope_limit: Finite generator identity only; does not verify all-state negative drift, recurrence, or uniformity.
